edits.value_json: The current graph 学 is arranged ⿳⺍冖子: ⺍ and 冖 together form an upper assembly above 子. This visible split does not settle how traditional 學 was first constructed. One account interprets oracle-bone forms as 𦥑 (two hands) with 五 and 六, while allowing that 爻 may supply a sound cue in some forms. Separate proposals describe associative forms involving 升 + 冖 or 林 + 冖; phonosemantic forms with 爻 as sound and 升 or 冖 as the other element; a rare element read jù, described as hands or claws and assigned both sound and meaning roles; and a distinct construction involving two 臼 forms with 冖. Another proposal says 子 was added in Western Zhou forms to mark a child learner. These are competing interpretations, not a settled reconstruction. The modern simplified shape does not establish the ancient structure.
学 means learning or study and is the standardized simplified counterpart of 學. Its upper assembly, ⺍ over 冖, sits above 子; these current parts do not settle the ancient construction.
